```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Everything in this chunk is given. Do not change it.
library(ggplot2)
library(jsonlite)
options(HTTPUserAgent = "3MB001-course", timeout = 60)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = TRUE, message = FALSE)

# Set to TRUE if an API is down: the report then uses the course copies.
use_snapshot <- FALSE

# Read a course copy: from your data/ folder, or else from the course site.
read_snapshot <- function(file) {
  local_file <- file.path("data", file)
  if (file.exists(local_file)) return(read.csv(local_file, check.names = FALSE))
  read.csv(paste0("https://henriksson-lab.github.io/course_cellbiology/",
                  "bioinfo-membrane-proteins/data/", file), check.names = FALSE)
}

# Where the data came from (filled in below).
gtex_source <- "GTEx v8, course copy retrieved 2026-11-18"
uniprot_source <- "UniProtKB, course copy retrieved 2026-11-18"
```

# 1. Where are the glucose transporters expressed?

SGLT1 (gene *SLC5A1*) and SGLT2 (gene *SLC5A2*) both move glucose with sodium.
This chunk asks the GTEx API for the median RNA level of each gene in every
tissue (unit: transcripts per million, TPM). It is given.

```{r fetch-gtex}
gtex_base <- "https://gtexportal.org/api/v2/"

fetch_gtex_gene <- function(gene) {
  # 1. Look up the gene's GENCODE ID used by GTEx v8.
  ref <- fromJSON(paste0(gtex_base, "reference/gene?geneId=", gene,
                         "&datasetId=gtex_v8"))$data
  gencode_id <- ref$gencodeId[ref$geneSymbol == gene][1]
  # 2. Fetch the median expression in every tissue.
  x <- fromJSON(paste0(gtex_base, "expression/medianGeneExpression?gencodeId=",
                       gencode_id, "&datasetId=gtex_v8"))$data
  data.frame(gene = gene, gencode_id = gencode_id,
             tissue = x$tissueSiteDetailId, median_tpm = x$median)
}

if (use_snapshot) {
  expression <- read_snapshot("gtex-medians-2026-11-18.csv")
} else {
  expression <- tryCatch({
    live <- rbind(fetch_gtex_gene("SLC5A1"), fetch_gtex_gene("SLC5A2"))
    gtex_source <- paste("GTEx v8 API, retrieved", Sys.Date())
    live
  }, error = function(e) read_snapshot("gtex-medians-2026-11-18.csv"))
}

expression$tissue <- gsub("_", " ", expression$tissue)
head(expression)
```

**Blank 1.** Keep only tissues where at least one of the two genes has a
median above `min_tpm`. Replace `___` with the value given on the course page.

```{r select-tissues}
min_tpm <- 10
plot_tissues <- unique(expression$tissue[expression$median_tpm > min_tpm])
plot_data <- expression[expression$tissue %in% plot_tissues, ]
length(plot_tissues)
```

**Blank 2.** Fill in the `aes()` mapping: put `median_tpm` on the x axis,
`tissue` on the y axis and colour the points by `gene`.

```{r expression-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = median_tpm, y = tissue, colour = gene)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Median RNA level (TPM)", y = NULL, colour = "Gene",
       caption = paste("Source:", gtex_source)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 2. How many times does each protein cross the membrane?

This chunk fetches the annotated transmembrane segments of eight membrane
proteins from UniProt and counts them. It is given.

```{r fetch-uniprot}
accessions <- c("P05023", "P11166", "P13866", "P31639",
                "P08183", "P13569", "P29972", "Q09470")
uniprot_url <- paste0("https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/accessions?accessions=",
                      paste(accessions, collapse = ","),
                      "&fields=accession,gene_primary,ft_transmem,length&format=tsv")

if (use_snapshot) {
  proteins <- read_snapshot("uniprot-features-2026-11-18.csv")
} else {
  proteins <- tryCatch({
    live <- read.delim(uniprot_url, check.names = FALSE, quote = "")
    uniprot_source <- paste("UniProtKB REST API, retrieved", Sys.Date())
    live
  }, error = function(e) read_snapshot("uniprot-features-2026-11-18.csv"))
}

proteins$gene <- proteins[["Gene Names (primary)"]]
# Each segment starts with the word "TRANSMEM"; count them.
proteins$tm_count <- lengths(regmatches(proteins$Transmembrane,
                                        gregexpr("TRANSMEM ", proteins$Transmembrane)))
proteins[, c("Entry", "gene", "tm_count")]
```

**Blank 3.** Fill in the y axis: the column that holds the number of segments.

```{r tm-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(proteins, aes(x = reorder(gene, tm_count), y = tm_count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#207a72") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Transmembrane segments (count)",
       caption = paste("Source:", uniprot_source)) +
  theme_minimal()
```
